newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends down on Tokyo, flat demand.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends down on Tokyo, flat demand.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended mixed after Tokyo futures fell in late trading and domestic demand remained flat, traders said.

At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board (MRELB) quoted market indicator price for November RSS 1 buyer at 308.50 cents ($1.23) a kg, down one cent down from Monday. November SMR 20 buyer was unchanged at 306.
Traders offered the SMR 20 at 305 cents, SMR 10 at 307, SMR 5 at 317, SMR L at 343, SMR CV at 363 and drum latex at 235.
Dealers said there were no incentives to move the market with the void in demand.
"I haven't heard of any buying for days and it looks like it'll stay like this for this week," said a dealer.

Dealers said the Malaysian rubber market was seeing extended bearishness after an active period of short-covering in recent months. Rains since early October have somehat reduced output from rubber plantations but sentiment remained weak, they said.
The INRO five-day average rose to 238.91 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Oct 22 from 238.72 on Oct 21. The daily indicator was unchanged at 238.95 against 238.98.
